definitions: To release or secure the release of (a person) from custody by providing security.
To scoop water out of (a boat or other vessel).
To make a sudden departure from a place or situation, often to avoid trouble or an undesirable outcome.
To make a parachute jump from an aircraft.
examples: The lawyer worked to bail his client out.
They had to bail water from the leaky boat.
He decided to bail on the meeting at the last minute.
The pilot had to bail out of the damaged plane.
